rules.statement: Do not put method bodies or logic, including extension methods with implementations, in an `*.Abstractions` package; keep it to contracts only and move helpers to an implementation or dependency-free helper package.
rules.why: An Abstractions package holds contracts only and no logic, so helpers with real bodies do not belong there.
rules.check: Look for new or moved classes in `*.Abstractions` projects that contain non-trivial method bodies, such as static extension classes or an `Extensions` folder holding logic.

rules.statement: Put general-purpose time helpers in the dependency-free `NCode.Time` package (namespace `NCode.Time`), not in JSON, JOSE or other feature packages.
rules.why: `NCode.Time` references only the base class library, so any package in the family can use it. Time helpers are not about JSON or a single feature.
rules.check: Look for new DateTime/DateTimeOffset/TimeProvider extension helpers added to packages other than `NCode.Time`, or helpers in `NCode.Json` or `NCode.Identity.*` that only deal with time.

rules.statement: When an instant must match an RFC 7519 NumericDate, truncate it to whole seconds with the shared `NCode.Time` helpers (`WithPrecisionInSeconds`, `GetUtcNowWithPrecisionInSeconds`, `GetTimestampWithPrecisionInSeconds`) and do not write the tick arithmetic inline.
rules.why: A time the server stores must equal the NumericDate it round-trips through a JWT. Repeating the truncation at many call sites lets one drift and store a time that no longer matches its token.
rules.check: Look for manual tick or millisecond truncation, such as `Ticks % TimeSpan.TicksPerSecond` or building a new DateTimeOffset from seconds, and for raw `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()` values stored next to token lifetimes or put into token claims.

rules.statement: Time-related tests use fixed instants rather than the wall clock, so results never depend on when the test runs.
rules.why: Tests that read the current time can depend on the exact millisecond they run at and become flaky.
rules.check: Look for `DateTime.Now`, `DateTime.UtcNow`, `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` or `TimeProvider.System` in tests of time logic, where a fixed instant or a fake TimeProvider should be used.
